evidence.note: Systematic environment probing before building: checks python3/node/npm, python version, pip list, attempts importing aiohttp/websockets/aiosqlite, then installs the missing deps. Confirms runtime constraints (Python 3.12 + playwright present, no web frameworks) before committing to an architecture.

Extracts resilience contract: plans a killable cross-node broadcaster with SQLite polling fallback, and identifies the node_id 0/1/2-to-port indexing and dense-seq-across-writers invariant as design drivers — mapping spec invariants onto architecture.

Explicit mid-build spec re-read: 'Actually re-reading: killing one HTTP node must not stop... IRC bridging on the other two' — revisits the contract and changes IRC placement (sed to run_irc=False, move to separate process) based on the re-read. Shows research steering implementation.

Contracts decomposed per subsystem into route files matching spec sections (routes_auth, routes_workspace with transfer_ownership as a distinct route, routes_channel, routes_message with reactions/replies, routes_groups, routes_invitations, ws with resume). Distinct transfer_ownership route suggests catching the PATCH-to-owner-rejected trap, but prose never enumerates subtler traps (member_user_ids naming, topic-not-from-description, non-member mention exclusion, resume.gap boundaries).

Verifies extracted invariants against runtime: confirms dense seq across nodes and that an IRC-committed message shares the same per-channel seq stream (seq=5), evidencing the seq contract was correctly mined and checked.

reasoning: The agent clearly confirmed the runtime (language/framework/browser/ports) before building and extracted the main contracts per subsystem, organizing route files to mirror the spec's sections and catching load-bearing invariants like dense-seq-across-writers, node_id indexing, and the resilience/broadcast-kill model — matching the level-5 anchor and exceeding it via one genuine mid-build spec re-read that changed the design (level-8 flavor). However, there is no living cross-referenced contract inventory of testids/IRC numerics/WS frame kinds, and the prose never surfaces the full set of subtle traps (member_user_ids vs members, topic auto-population, non-member mention exclusion, resume.gap boundaries), so it falls short of the 8/10 anchors. This places it at a 6: solid per-subsystem extraction plus real environment probing, but not the systematic, self-correcting contract map of the top anchors.
